models.title: Gear cutter

One master station takes the temporal gear (12 teeth, the size of the game's gears) or the large temporal gear (20). The feed's rectifier, clutch, worm and wheel are enclosed in the column and a gearbox with removable covers; a sight-feed drip oiler over the cutter shows the machine's oil. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/GearCutter/tools/make_shape.py.

models.title: Draw bench
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's draw bench, one block wide and four long: a chain draw bench that draws a lead or copper hollow section (the game's chute section), threaded on a mandrel, through a die into four pipe sections, a quarter of it a stroke. The dog grips each section's point at the die and an endless chain beside the bed, shackled to it, hauls it along, driven from the axle through a rectifier, a cone clutch and a two-speed change gear (copper draws at half lead's speed). Each section is handed out as its draw finishes and the jaws open, the dog knocks the clutch out at the end of its stroke, and a counterweight hauls the chain and the dog back. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/DrawBench/tools/make_shape.py.

models.title: Cylinder borer
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's cylinder borer, one block wide, two high and four long, after John Wilkinson's boring mill of 1775. What it bores is the cylinder of Pipes and Power Expanded's Watt and Cornish engines (their engine block's barrel: 10 voxels across, its bore 8, 16 long, a band near its top and two steam ports), cast in iron for the Watt or in steel for the Cornish, as ppex draws them. The casting, square outside as ppex draws it and with a round bore, lies on its side on two timber bearers, chained down, and a slender boring bar runs right through it, carried in a bushing at each end and turned from the axle through a pinion and a great wheel, 1:4. A cutter head keyed on the bar is drawn through the bore by a control rod from a crosshead on the bench's ways, pulled by a rope wound on a drum that a falling weight turns: a weighted feed, as Wilkinson's was. The cast skin sinks into the wall as the cutters pass, leaving the bore bright. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/CylinderBorer/tools/make_shape.py.
models.credit: Made for the Seraph Horizons mod; no other mod's model is used. The cylinder is drawn to the proportions of Pipes and Power Expanded's engine cylinder, in the game textures its engines wear.

models.title: Press brake
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's press brake, one block wide and two long: a hand-worked leaf brake (cornice brake) of the early 1800s in oak with iron wearing edges and cupronickel screws. models.title: Mandrel forging station
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's mandrel forging station, one block wide and two long: a smith's station of the 1700s, an oak stump carrying an iron mandrel in a bracket, with a small swage beside it. A lead or copper hollow section is hammered down onto the mandrel blow by blow: it closes from 8 to 6 across onto the mandrel and stretches from 8 to 16 long, evenly, into one tube, two pipe sections end to end. Or a hot steel rod laid along the mandrel is wound round it from the shoulder, a side at a time, each growing from its corner as the rod shrinks into it, into a six-turn square coil spring. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/MandrelStation/tools/make_shape.py.
models.credit: Made for the Seraph Horizons mod; no other mod's model is used.

The model is posed by the work below, which Play moves with it at a lead hollow's nine turns (in the game copper takes fourteen blows, and a spring eight turns: 1.125 RPS shows a spring at the game's pace)

work.label: Work
work.hint: A hollow: it closes from 8 to 6 across onto the mandrel and stretches from 8 to 16 long, evenly, into one tube, its two pipe sections end to end; at 1 it is on the mandrel and the game delivers the sections. A spring: the rod lies straight along the mandrel's top edge, the coil's length; each side grows from its corner along its own line across the face, as wire laid down, while the rod moves across that face with the growing end, its shoulder end at the bend, shrinking into the coil; so the rod goes round the mandrel a face a side, never stopping, used up from the shoulder while its far end stays put, and the coil grows from the shoulder a pitch a turn; at 1 the spring is wound, the rod gone, and the game delivers it.

models.title: Amalgam pan
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's amalgam pan, one block: an amalgamating pan of the mid 1800s, the Washoe process's pan scaled down, worked as the quern is, by hand or by an axle from below. A shallow sheet-iron pan on an oak stand with a hollow cast-iron cone in its floor, and two parts fitted to it by hand: the muller, an iron spindle (the fitted rod) with a hub and four arms, which comes down through the cone and a footstep on an oak bridge-tree to the vanilla axle's cross profile at the block's bottom face, where an axle in the block below turns it; then its shoes, a plate under each arm's end dragging on the floor, in the plate's metal. The shoes work crushed gold or silver quartz, water and mercury into a pulp, and the mercury takes up the free gold or silver as amalgam. A thin film of water can stand over the charge, swept round with the muller and parted round each shoe. The player loads it and empties it by hand, with no chute or hopper. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/AmalgamPan/tools/make_shape.py.
models.credit: Made for the Seraph Horizons mod; no other mod's model is used. The mercury is drawn as Expanded Matter draws it, from the game's own rock textures; the slurry's texture is the mod's own.

models.title: Eidolon gantry
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's eidolon gantry, six blocks deep, five wide and five and a half high: an open timber frame in the wood it is built from (oak here), with iron plates, brackets and pegs, in which the eidolon is built stage by stage, hung limp from a hand winch at the back, geared in wood like a mill, whose chain runs over a sheave on the hoist beam and whose crank is outside the frame, on the south side; it stays as the eidolon's dock, and the front (west) is open for it to walk out of. The frame is crafted and the winch fitted onto it stage by stage, from vanilla's wooden axles and spur gears, planks, iron and chain. The chain then hangs a wooden spine by a ring over its top peg, empty; the crafted torso is placed onto it first and the body built on in layers, and when the eidolon wakes it unclamps, steps forward off it and leaves it hanging empty; it docks back onto it to have its layers stripped and refitted. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/EidolonGantry/tools/make_shape.py.
models.credit: The gantry, its winch and chains were made for the Seraph Horizons mod. The body hung in it and the spine it hangs from are Anego Studios' model, Vintage Story's mobile eidolon, posed in its hung animation; they are not covered by the repository's license.

models.title: Crucible furnace
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's crucible furnace, three blocks wide, three deep and two high: one Huntsman (Sheffield) melting hole of the late nineteenth century, centred in thick walls of fired brick of any one type, lined on its hot faces with tier-3 refractory brick and bound with iron, holding two fireclay pots side by side on a grate of firebars, packed round in one bed of coke to their shoulders, under a hinged lid of firebrick in an iron frame that swings back on its top back edge to rest just past upright against two iron stops; shut, it lies flush with the floor. Natural draught only: air comes in at the ash mouth in the middle of the front, under the grate, which an iron damper slides over (open, half, shut), and leaves by a flue to an outlet in the middle of the back row, where the player stands the chimney or a flat iron cap. Built in stages: the iron frame, the brickwork, the lining, the lid and damper. Furnaces stand side by side in a row of up to five, fifteen blocks long, their plain side walls meeting, sharing one chimney. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/CrucibleFurnace/tools/make_shape.py.
models.credit: Made for the Seraph Horizons mod; no other mod's model is used.

models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's riddle, one block: a miner's hand riddle of the 1800s, the hand station that classifies crushed ore. A square, shallow sieve after vanilla's pan (two stepped tiers of oak boards) with a coarse woven mesh of iron wire, resting by its north and south boards on two oak bearers across a plank box whose corners are bound with nailed angle-iron straps. models.title: Stamp battery
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's stamp battery, three blocks wide, four high and three deep: the ore line's crushing and classifying machine, a wet five-stamp gravity battery in an oak frame, its footprint fixed from the frame on. The vanilla axle drives a closed rectifier gear case at the back, whose line shaft belts the bull pulley on the camshaft: involute cams lift each stamp and let it fall onto its die in the mortar, in the order 1-3-5-2-4. The crushed ore splashes out through the mesh screen straight into a funnel of the chute's sheet as wide as the screen, which narrows to a stub of the game's own chute flush with the front face; ore comes in by chute from above, or by hand at the same mouth, through a chute section in the top face into the plank feed box behind the mortar, so a chute line can feed it and another take its pulp away. The water line comes in at the west face as Pipes and Power Expanded's pipe and, through a soldered reducer, runs on as a small pipe in copper or lead to a header along the mortar's back: a branch to each stamp, each with a bronze cock, discharges into the mortar through the feed opening, behind the stamp's shoe, and the water washes the crushed ore out through the screen. The frame is placed, its oak sills with the gear case and the line shaft, then it is built in five stages: the timber, the end frames, girts, ties and bearers, fitted a stack at a time; the mortar; the stamps, hung in their guides; the camshaft, its cams set to the hung stamps, with its belt and the feed box; and services, every chute section and the water line. The shoes are the wearing part. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/StampBattery/tools/make_shape.py.

models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's arrastra: a mule-sized drag-stone mill, the ore line's small grinder, worked in batches by hand. models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's sluice, one block wide and four long: the riffled plank sluice of a stamp mill of the 1890s, the first concentrator of the ore line. The pulp comes down a vanilla copper chute into a plank head box, where a ppex water pipe, soldered in copper or lead, comes in under the box and rises through its floor to a nozzle; it overflows a sill onto a plank trough falling 1 in 12 on three trestles, across whose floor, over the second and third blocks, seven oak riffles faced with strap iron hold back the heavy grains. The concentrate is drawn off as it settles, through a slot in the floor behind each riffle, into a launder slung under the sluice that falls with it and pours, past the last riffle, straight down the concentrate chute, which stands upright in the third block and leaves through its bottom face into a chute below; the rest runs on over the fourth block's plain floor and off the tail into the tailings chute on its south end. It takes no power, nothing moves, and nothing is cleaned up by hand. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/Sluice/tools/make_shape.py.

models.title: Reverberatory roaster
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's reverberatory roaster (#737), three blocks wide, two high and five long with the drive's row on its roof: a long, low furnace under a curved arch, the fire at the north end thrown over a bridge wall and along a flat hearth where the sulfide concentrate lies, and up an uptake at the south end to the outlet the chimney stands on. It is the mechanical furnace: two water-cooled rabbles on spindles through the arch, turned by bevel gears from a line shaft on the roof behind a rectifying gear case, plough the charge from the feed at the flue end to the discharge hole by the bridge; a fluted feed roll under the hopper meters the charge in, a coal bunker in the fire end's top feeds a step grate, natural draught comes in at the ash mouth under its three-place damper, and ppex water is narrowed through the vanner's soldered reducer to a small pipe to swivels on the spindles. The work doors on the east stay shut (kept for clearing accretions), the first with a peep hole through which its rabble is seen turning. The brickwork takes any fired brick, the hot faces are lined with tier-3 refractory brick and the arch is that refractory; the west wall is plain and flush, so two stand back to back sharing it, one outlet capped. The brick is bound in angle iron set in flush, one closed box frame following its outline: an angle up every outside corner, knees where the footing steps out, and a band along every top edge (the end faces', the shared wall's, the end blocks' and the footing's, and over the arch's bay a skewback angle the east side's length and bands round the arch's ends), with the buckstays and tie rods joining it. It is built in stages, the vanilla chute's sections and the water pipes last. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/ReverberatoryRoaster/tools/make_shape.py.

models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's cupellation furnace, three blocks wide, two high and two deep, with its stack in a column behind the west end: an English cupellation (test) furnace of the nineteenth century in thick walls of fired brick of any one type, lined on its hot faces with tier-3 refractory brick and bound with angle iron in one frame, an angle up each outside corner carrying an angle band round the top, the bands butted at every corner. Side by side, the test (an oval of bone ash in an iron ring, standing on the hearth of a low chamber under a stepped vault) and the fireplace (coal on a grate of firebars behind a fire bridge, over an ash pit with an iron damper, open, half or shut, over its ash mouth). The flame crosses the bridge and the test and leaves by a flue in the back wall to the stack and its outlet on the top, where the player stands the chimney or a flat iron cap. Coal is fed by hand through the fire door. The blast comes by pipe: Steelmaking Expanded's engine air blower, on a steam engine, puts air into the pipe network, and a pipe laid to the socket in the middle of the back wall (a short copper stub of the pipe, flanged to the wind box's plate in an iron-lined pocket, its mouth soldered as Seraph Horizons' copper and lead pipes are, flush with the wall: one fixed connector, drawing 10 litres of air a second at 1.5 atm or more) feeds an iron wind box and the tuyere, which blows across the lead towards the front, where the litharge runs out through a gate in the test's breast, along an iron gutter through the working door's sill, into a pot in a bay of the front face. Built in stages: the iron frame, the brickwork, the lining, the fittings (with the test's iron ring), and last the test, the wearing part: its bone ash, broken out and beaten in afresh every 15 charges. models.title: Ball mill
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's ball mill, three blocks long, two high and two deep: a Krupp (Gruson) ball mill of the 1890s, the ore line's continuous grinder. A short drum on a hollow trunnion and a journal, in two bearings on cast pedestals on a masonry bed, in which iron balls (not drawn) tumble over the ore and grind it; round the drum and turning with it the screens, a coarse one of perforated plate and a fine one of wire cloth, which let out only what is ground fine enough into the discharge hopper under them, and from it by the output chute. The axle drives a stainless pinion on its own line, which turns the drum at a third of the axle, whichever way, by a wooden girth wheel: oak cogs mortised through two courses of oak felloes, bolted to a cast flange on the drum's journal. Ore comes in by a chute into the feed box at the trunnion's mouth, water by a ppex pipe beside it, and the box's spout runs into the trunnion's bore. Its frame, the bed, pedestals and bearings, is placed; then it is built in five stages: the drum; the gearing (the girth wheel, then the pinion); the screens; the sheet iron, the hopper and the feed box; and services, the chute sections and the water pipe in copper or lead. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/BallMill/tools/make_shape.py.

models.title: Amalgamation plates
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's amalgamation plates, one block wide, one high and three long: a plate table of the 1890s stamp mill as a machine of its own. An oak-trestled plank bed falling 1 in 10 carries three copper plates dressed with mercury; at the head a distributor under the infeed chute spreads the crushed ore across their width through a row of holes, and a spray pipe across the head washes onto them: soldered copper or lead pipe of Pipes and Power Expanded, narrowed from ppex's full pipe through a soldered reducer to a small spray pipe, as on the vanner. The plates are dressed with mercury as a recurring job, not a build stage. The pulp runs down the plates in a thin sheet, the free gold and silver that touch them are held as amalgam, which builds up on the plates to be scraped off by hand, and the rest falls off the foot into a tail box and out by chute. It is built in three stages: the table and plates; a mercury trap in the tail box, a cast-iron well with a hanging baffle the pulp passes under and a weir it passes over; and services, the chute sections and the water line. No power: a plate table works by gravity, and nothing moves. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/AmalgamationPlates/tools/make_shape.py.

models.title: Jig
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's jig, one block wide, two high and two deep: a Harz plunger jig of the later nineteenth century. A plank box of water, the hutch, bound at its corners with nailed angle-iron straps, is divided across by a partition open below it: the sieve compartment at the front, the plunger compartment behind. An eccentric on the jig's own shaft, turned by an axle at the back, works the plunger up and down through an iron yoke, and each stroke pulses the water up through the ore bed on the sieve: the heavy grains sink through into the hutch, slide down its sloping bottom and leave by an iron spout through the front wall's foot into the concentrate chute; the light ones are carried along the sieve from the head end, where the feed trough drops the ore, to the tail end, and over the weir's iron lip through a port in the tail end's head into the tailings chute. The ore comes in by chute from above onto the feed trough, the water by a ppex pipe into the plunger compartment. The hutch's sills and plank floor are placed as the frame, and the rest is built in four stages: the hutch's timber, its walls, partition, ledges and sloping bottom with the iron that binds them, fitted a stack at a time; the sieve; the drive and plunger; and services, the chutes and the water inlet in copper or lead. models.title: Shaking table
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's shaking table, two blocks wide, one high and three long: a Wilfley table of about 1900, the ore line's third concentrator. A riffled deck, tilted a little across its width, slides on iron plates on an oak stand, shaken along its length by a differential head in a closed cast-iron box: a slow push towards the far end and a quick pull back, so the heavy grains walk along the riffles while the wash water carries the light ones across to the low side. The axle drives the head through a closed rectifier case (3:1 up), so the deck strokes the same whichever way the axle turns; a flywheel turns on the head shaft. The ore comes in by chute to the feed box, the wash water by soldered pipe to the water box along the upper edge; the concentrate leaves off the far end, the middlings off its lower corner and the tailings off the low side, each by launder to a chute. It is built in four stages on its placed frame: the deck, the rectifier, the differential head (whose shaft's first bearing is the rectifier's boss and whose rod pins into the deck), and services, the chutes and the water line in copper or lead. models.title: Vanner
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's vanner, two blocks wide, three long and one high: a Frue vanner (1874), the last of the ore line's concentrators. An endless stitched leather belt four feet wide, raised edges all round it, on a head and a foot roller twelve feet apart, falling gently to the foot, on a frame that six pinned uprights carry and two eccentrics on a countershaft along its side shake across once a turn of the axle. A fixed pawl pushes a ratchet on the worm shaft a tooth each stroke, and the worm's helical thread, running in the teeth of a worm wheel on the head roller, creeps the belt round its rollers at the head drum's surface speed, its top run up to the head, whichever way the axle turns: its two laced seams travel round the loop with it, slowly (about 855 turns of the axle once round). Pulp from the infeed chute spills from the feed box onto the belt; a spray pipe near the head washes it; the heavy grains ride over the head into the concentrate box and its chute, the light ones run off the foot into the tailings box and its chute. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/Vanner/tools/make_shape.py.

models.title: Stall roaster
models.description: The Seraph Horizons mod's stall roaster, two blocks wide, two deep and two high: one roasting stall of the late nineteenth century, a bay of fired brick of any one type open at the front and to the sky, lined with tier-3 refractory brick on its floor and its inner faces, and bound with one frame of angle iron that wraps its corners: an angle up each outer corner and each jamb of the opening (on each side wall's narrow front face the corner's and the jamb's legs meet, casing the wall's end in iron), a sill angle along the opening's foot down to the ground, and angle bands round all four top edges, joining the angles' tops; no sliver of brick shows between two irons. Sulfide rock is charged by hand through the front in four courses of eight on a bed of firewood, kindled at the bed, and left to roast for days on its own sulfur; the front is walled up with loose brick, open, half or whole, its bottom course left with two draught holes, which sets the draught; the air goes back through the charge into a flue mouth at the foot of the back wall, along a back flue and up a stack to an outlet on the top, where the player stands the chimney or a flat iron cap. Sulfur collects in the heap's crust; native sulfur rock is melted out the same way, lit from above. Nothing moves and it takes no power. Built in stages: the iron frame, the brickwork, the lining. Stalls stand side by side in a row of up to six, their side walls meeting, sharing one chimney. Generated by mods-src/seraphhorizons/StallRoaster/tools/make_shape.py.
